title: All the Housing Changes Announced at the National Day Rally 2026 Speech
summary: PM Lawrence Wong announced several housing changes during Singapore’s 2026 National Day Rally. Find out what they could mean for your next property move.
body_markdown:
Last Updated on August 26, 2026 byYolly Del Prado


At this year’s[National Day Rally on 23 August 2026](https://www.pmo.gov.sg/newsroom/ndr2026/) , Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced higher income ceilings for HDB flat and EC buyers, additional BTO and SBF ballot chances for first-timer families with children, and a revised date for the final BTO exercise of 2026.


For buyers, however, the useful question is what these changes alter. A higher ceiling may bring an HDB flat or new EC back into consideration, but it does not automatically make that home affordable. An extra ballot chance improves your position, but it is not a queue number.


Here is what changed, who may benefit and what remains the same.


---


## Table of Contents:


- National Day Rally 2026 Housing Changes at a Glance
- HDB Income Ceilings Raised to $16,000 for Families and $8,000 for Singles
- Income Ceiling Raised to $18,000 for Qualifying New EC Units
- Income Ceilings Also Raised for PPHS, Second-timer and Senior Housing Schemes
- More Children Will Mean More BTO and SBF Ballot Chances
- The October 2026 BTO Exercise Has Been Moved to November
- More Housing Support is Being Considered for Larger Families, Singles and Seniors
- What Should Buyers Do Next?
- Frequently Asked Questions


---


## National Day Rally 2026 Housing Changes at a Glance


**Change** **Who it affects** **Key timing or condition**


Family income ceiling rises from $14,000 to $16,000 Eligible families buying a subsidised HDB flat, buying a resale flat with the CPF Housing Grant or applying for an HDB loan HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) applications made on or after 24 August 2026


Singles’ income ceiling rises from $7,000 to $8,000 Eligible single buyers aged 35 and above HFE applications made on or after 24 August 2026


New EC income ceiling rises from $16,000 to $18,000 Eligible households buying qualifying new EC units Projects with land-sale tender closing dates on or after 24 August 2026


Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS), Fresh Start and Step-Up income ceilings rise from $7,000 to $8,000 Eligible PPHS applicants and second-timer families under the Fresh Start Housing Scheme or Step-Up CPF Housing Grant Other conditions for the respective schemes continue to apply


Income ceiling for selected senior schemes rises from $14,000 to $16,000 Eligible seniors under the Lease Buyback Scheme, Silver Housing Bonus, Community Care Apartments or short-lease 2-room Flexi scheme Other conditions for the respective schemes continue to apply


One additional ballot chance for every eligible child First-timer families with children or expecting a child All BTO and Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) applications from the February 2027 sales exercise


October BTO exercise moves to November Buyers planning to apply in the final BTO exercise of 2026 Applicants are advised to submit their HFE documents by 25 September 2026


## HDB Income Ceilings Raised to $16,000 for Families and $8,000 for Singles


[From 24 August 2026](https://www.mnd.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/view/increase-in-income-ceilings-and-greater-support-for-families-with-children) , the monthly household income ceiling is $16,000 for eligible families and $8,000 for eligible singles aged 35 and above. Previously, the limits were $14,000 and $7,000 respectively.


For families, the $16,000 ceiling can apply when buying a new subsidised HDB flat, purchasing a resale flat with the CPF Housing Grant or applying for an HDB loan. The corresponding $8,000 ceiling applies to eligible singles.


An income ceiling is an entry condition, not a promise of assistance. Your HFE letter will still determine whether you can buy an HDB flat, which grants you may receive and whether you qualify for an HDB loan.


There is also an easily missed resale detail. The new limits are not a blanket ceiling for every HDB resale purchase.[HDB states](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/couples-and-families) that there is no income ceiling for eligible families buying an unclassified or Standard resale flat without CPF housing grants or an HDB loan. Limits still apply where a grant, HDB financing or the flat’s classification requires them.


This means a household that remains above the new ceiling may still be able to buy certain resale HDB flats. The trade-off is that it may have to proceed without the relevant grants or an HDB loan, subject to the other purchase conditions.


## Income Ceiling Raised to $18,000 for Qualifying New EC Units


The monthly household income ceiling for a new EC has risen from $16,000 to $18,000, helping households previously above the limit.


However, the $18,000 ceiling applies only to new units in EC projects whose land-sale tenders close on or after 24 August 2026. Existing EC balance units and projects tied to earlier tenders are excluded.


A household earning $17,000 therefore does not become eligible for every new EC currently on the market. Check the development’s land-sale tender date instead of relying on whether the unit is described as “new”.


Resale ECs are separate transactions and are not covered by this announcement. The revised ceiling concerns qualifying new EC units sold by developers, not EC homes being resold by their owners.


Even for a qualifying new EC, staying within the income ceiling is only one requirement. Citizenship, family nucleus, property ownership and other EC eligibility rules still apply. Buyers will also need to consider the downpayment, loan limits and monthly repayments before deciding whether an EC is comfortable for their finances.


## Income Ceilings Also Raised for PPHS, Second-timer and Senior Housing Schemes


The revised income ceilings extend beyond the buyers looking for a subsidised HDB flat or new EC.


The monthly household income ceiling for the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme will increase from $7,000 to $8,000. The same adjustment applies to eligible second-timer families under the Fresh Start Housing Scheme and Step-Up CPF Housing Grant.


For eligible seniors, the ceiling rises from $14,000 to $16,000 for the Lease Buyback Scheme, Silver Housing Bonus and the purchase of a Community Care Apartment or short-lease 2-room Flexi flat.


These may not be the most widely discussed parts of the announcement, but they matter to households planning around temporary accommodation, a second chance at home ownership or retirement.


## More Children Will Mean More BTO and SBF Ballot Chances


From the February 2027 sales exercise, first-timer families with children or expecting a child will receive one additional ballot chance for each Singapore Citizen child aged 18 and below. The change applies to all Build-To-Order and Sale of Balance Flats applications.


“Additional” is important here. These chances sit on top of the chances for which the family already qualifies; they are not the family’s total number of ballot chances.


**Family situation** **Additional ballot chances**


One eligible child +1 chance


Two eligible children +2 chances


Three eligible children +3 chances


First-timer families expecting a child can qualify too. More chances do not reserve a flat or guarantee success. Results still depend on demand, available units and other priority rules, so families should continue comparing location, waiting time and price.


The timing matters as well. Families applying before the February 2027 exercise will not receive these additional chances under the new measure. Those deciding between an earlier opportunity and waiting for the new rules will need to weigh the value of an extra chance against the availability of suitable projects.


## The October 2026 BTO Exercise Has Been Moved to November


The next BTO exercise will be held in November 2026 instead of October. The additional time allows buyers to review their housing plans and apply for an HFE letter under the revised income ceilings.


HDB and the Ministry of National Development have advised buyers to apply early and submit all required HFE documents by 25 September 2026. This is an advised submission date, not a reason to wait until the last day.


About 7,970 flats are expected across Bedok, Geylang, Sembawang, Tengah, Toa Payoh and Yishun, with Community Care Apartments in Toa Payoh. Project classifications will be confirmed at launch.


Compare the locations in our[November 2026 BTO launch guide](https://ohmyhome.com/en-sg/blog/the-complete-guide-to-the-october-2026-bto-launch-sites-what-buyers-should-know/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=backlink&utm_campaign=NDP2026HousingChanges) for a closer look at the planned projects, flat types and surrounding amenities.


## More Housing Support is Being Considered for Larger Families, Singles and Seniors


Three other housing directions were mentioned during the Rally, although they are not new policies yet.


Prime Minister Lawrence Wong asked for further housing support for larger families to be considered. He also said the Government intends to take further steps to support singles with housing within this term.


In addition, the Government is working on ways to make it easier for seniors to unlock value from their homes for retirement while continuing to live in them.


No specific eligibility conditions, grant amounts or implementation dates have been announced for these plans. Buyers should therefore wait for the details before including any potential benefit in their housing decisions.


No new Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD), Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD), loan-to-value or rental rules were announced during the Rally.


## What Should Buyers Do Next?


The announcements create more routes into housing, but eligibility only tells you which doors are open. Your budget, location, waiting time and family plans should decide which one is worth walking through.


If your income previously placed you just above an HDB limit, start by applying for an HFE letter under the revised ceiling. If you are considering an EC, confirm that the development qualifies for the $18,000 ceiling. Meanwhile, families weighing BTO and SBF applications should note that the additional ballot chances begin only in February 2027.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How does HDB calculate household income for an HFE letter?


HDB generally assesses the average gross monthly income of all applicants and occupiers for the months worked during a 12-month assessment period. The period ends two months before the HFE application month. Required documents depend on each person’s employment type.


### Can a single person buy a new Executive Condominium in Singapore?


A single person cannot buy a new EC alone. Under the Joint Singles Scheme, two or more Singapore Citizen singles aged at least 35 may apply together, subject to the combined income ceiling and all other EC eligibility conditions. Alternatively, a single Singapore Citizen or PR may buy a[resale EC after its Minimum Occupation Period (MOP)](https://ohmyhome.com/en-sg/blog/what-you-should-know-about-the-new-ec-rules-in-2026/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=backlink&utm_campaign=NDP2026HousingChanges) .


### Does the Proximity Housing Grant have an income ceiling?


No. The Proximity Housing Grant has no income ceiling. Eligible families and singles buying a resale HDB flat to live with or near their parents or children may qualify, provided they meet the proximity, citizenship and other grant conditions.
